subject: biology
title: Kingdoms Plantae and Animalia
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: Practice set for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a characteristic feature of flatworms (Platyhelminthes)?
questions.answer: D

questions.q: Which of them is a true fish?
questions.answer: A

questions.q: Bryophytes are called the amphibians of the plant kingdom because —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: The dominant phase of a fern is —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: The fruit of Poaceae is —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: The stamens of the pea flower are —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: Cnidoblasts are present in —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: The excretory organs of earthworm are —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: The class of animals with a four-chambered heart and pneumatic bones is —
questions.answer: A

questions.answer: A

questions.answer: A

questions.answer: A

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Match: (a) Malvaceae (b) Fabaceae (c) Poaceae with (i) Pisum sativum (ii) Hibiscus rosa-sinensis (iii) Oryza sativa.
Fill in the blanks: (a) The male sex organ of bryophytes is the ______. (b) The spore-bearing structures of a fern occur in groups called ______.
questions.answer: (a) antheridium. (b) sori.

questions.q: State true or false: (a) Gymnosperms have seeds enclosed in an ovary. (b) The fern prothallus is a gametophyte.
questions.answer: (a) False – the seeds are naked. (b) True.

questions.q: Name the phylum: (a) tube feet (b) cnidoblasts.
questions.answer: (a) Echinodermata. (b) Cnidaria.

questions.q: Give the number of stamens in: (a) Fabaceae (b) Liliaceae.
Give the botanical name of (a) rice (b) wheat.
questions.answer: (a) Oryza sativa. (b) Triticum aestivum.

questions.q: Name one example each: (a) liverwort (b) moss.
questions.answer: (a) Marchantia. (b) Funaria.

questions.q: Give the number of heart chambers in (a) a frog (b) a crocodile.
questions.answer: (a) Three. (b) Four.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: With reference to class Reptilia, identify the two wrong statements: (a) Body is covered by hairs (b) Paired pentadactyl limbs with clawed digits (c) Respiration by lungs (d) Heart is two chambered.
questions.answer: (a) and (d) are wrong. The body of reptiles is covered by dry horny scales, not hair, and the heart is three-chambered (four-chambered in crocodiles), not two-chambered.

questions.q: With the help of suitable diagrams differentiate between the androecium in pea and china rose.
questions.answer: Pea (Fabaceae): 10 stamens, diadelphous (9 fused in one bundle and 1 free). China rose (Malvaceae): numerous stamens fused by their filaments into a staminal tube (monadelphous).

questions.q: Write two differences between gymnosperms and angiosperms.
questions.answer: Gymnosperm seeds are naked (borne on cones) and xylem lacks vessels; angiosperm seeds are enclosed in fruits and xylem has vessels.

questions.q: Write any two general characters of phylum Arthropoda.
questions.answer: Jointed legs and a chitinous exoskeleton, with a segmented body divided into head, thorax and abdomen.

questions.q: Why are sponges classed as the lowest animals?
questions.answer: They are asymmetrical, have a cellular grade of organisation without tissues or organs, and have a canal system.

questions.q: List two economic importance of gymnosperms.
questions.answer: They yield timber and resins or turpentine; chilgoza (dry fruit) and sago from Cycas.

questions.q: Distinguish between cartilaginous and bony fishes (any two points).
questions.answer: Cartilaginous fishes (Scoliodon) have a cartilaginous skeleton, ventral mouth and no operculum; bony fishes (Labeo) have a bony skeleton, terminal mouth and an operculum.

questions.q: Name the two subkingdoms of Animalia and give their basis.
questions.answer: Parazoa (no tissues, cellular grade, e.g. sponges) and Eumetazoa (tissue or organ grades of organisation).

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Write the characteristic features of Bryophyta.
questions.answer: They are non-vascular embryophytes; the independent plant body is the haploid gametophyte; it has rhizoids but no true roots, stems or leaves; sex organs are antheridia and archegonia surrounded by a sterile jacket; the dependent sporophyte produces spores by meiosis.

questions.q: Describe the main features of the family Fabaceae.
questions.answer: Zygomorphic, bisexual flowers; five sepals; five papilionaceous petals (standard, two wings and two keel petals); ten diadelphous stamens; monocarpellary superior ovary with marginal placentation; the fruit is a pod; examples are pea and gram.

questions.q: Give the main characteristics of the family Malvaceae.
questions.answer: Actinomorphic pentamerous flowers with an epicalyx; five free petals; numerous monadelphous stamens joined into a staminal tube; five syncarpous carpels with axile placentation; fruit a capsule; e.g. Hibiscus, cotton, bhindi.

questions.q: Write the characters of Aves.
questions.answer: They are warm-blooded with feathers, a beak without teeth, pneumatic bones, forelimbs modified into wings, a four-chambered heart, a syrinx and only the left ovary, and they lay shelled eggs.

questions.q: Write any three characters of Phylum Platyhelminthes with examples.
questions.answer: Dorsoventrally flattened and acoelomate, with a gut that has a single opening or is absent; mostly parasitic; examples are Planaria, Fasciola and Taenia.

questions.q: List the distinguishing features of Mammalia.
questions.answer: Hair on the body, mammary glands, external ears (pinnae), heterodont and thecodont dentition, four-chambered heart, diaphragm and viviparity.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Classify the Kingdom Plantae into divisions with their main characteristics.
questions.answer: Bryophyta: non-vascular, gametophyte dominant. Pteridophyta: vascular, sporophyte dominant, spores in sori. Spermatophyta: seed plants, divided into gymnosperms (naked seeds, cones) and angiosperms (seeds in fruits; dicots with two cotyledons and monocots with one).

questions.q: Distinguish between dicots and monocots.
questions.answer: Seed with two versus one cotyledon; tap root versus fibrous root; reticulate versus parallel venation; flowers pentamerous versus trimerous; vascular bundles in a ring, open and collateral versus scattered and closed.

questions.q: Classify phylum Arthropoda into classes with examples.
questions.answer: Arachnida (cephalothorax, four pairs of legs; scorpion), Crustacea (cephalothorax with carapace; prawn), Myriapoda (many segments with 1-2 pairs of legs each; centipede, millipede) and Insecta (head, thorax with three pairs of legs and wings, abdomen; cockroach).

questions.q: Describe the characteristic features of the classes Amphibia and Reptilia.
questions.answer: Amphibia: live on land and in water, moist glandular skin, no claws, three-chambered heart, eggs laid in water, gills in larva and lungs in adult (frog). Reptilia: dry scaly skin, clawed digits, lungs, three-chambered heart with a partial septum (four in crocodile), leathery shelled eggs on land (lizard, snake).

questions.q: Describe the basis for the classification of animals.
questions.answer: Level of organisation, symmetry, body cavity, number of germ layers and presence of the notochord, with examples of each category.
